Higgsfield Videos

How we take a video that already works and make it hers, in her niche: Higgsfield puts her in the video, CapCut adds the music and the text hook. Watch the Loom first, then follow this step by step.

tutorial link

02What this is

We take a video that already did very well on social media (raw, made by a real creator) and remake it with her: her alone, or her with friends, whatever the original has. Then we make it belong to her niche.

The 3 things that make it hers1 · Outfits from her niche (Higgsfield).
2 · Music that fits her niche (CapCut).
3 · Text hook: the words on screen that stop the scroll (CapCut).

Keep what made the original work: the motion, the energy, the setting, the variety. Change only what makes it hers.

Why this works: the original already proved people stop and watch it. We keep the part that grabbed them and point it at her fans. Learning to see why a video works is the real skill here: it’s instinct, pattern recognition and emotion, and it grows with every video you make.

03Before you start

  • Higgsfield open on the laptop. Log in with your Santor Google account (your Santor Gmail). K hasn’t given you one yet? Use K’s email to practise: ask K.
  • CapCut installed on the laptop.
  • The Factory open: Idea Bank, Song library, Reference library.
  • Your task: the video to remake, or "pick one from the Idea Bank".

04Step by step: a simple video

1

Pick the original

Your task gives you a video, or K or Leon sends one on Slack. If not, pick one from the Idea Bank: videos we saved because they did very well.

Idea Bank: santor-media.up.railway.app/higgs · older ideas: santor-media.up.railway.app/prompts#ideas

Once you’ve learnt winning videos, you join the ideas group chat. Send videos you think would work for her; the good ones go into the Idea Bank. the group chat

2

Watch it: why does it work?

Watch it once, as a fan would. Then say in one sentence why it works: what makes you stop? The girls, the outfits, the setting, the noise, the moment something happens?

K’s example: several girls in sexy outfits, lots of noise, and you feel like you’re in the elevator with them.

Why: that sentence tells you what to keep. If you can’t say why it works, you’ll change the wrong thing.

3

Download it

From the Idea Bank or Slack: press Download.

Found it somewhere else, like Instagram? Download it with an Instagram downloader: copy the post’s link, paste it in, download. which downloader

4

Higgsfield → Genjutsu

In Higgsfield: Video → Genjutsu. Check Motion transfer is selected. Clear anything left from before. Press the empty box to add the reference video.

Why: Genjutsu takes a real video and puts our people and outfits inside it. The motion stays exactly the same.

5

Upload the original

Press Upload media, pick the video you downloaded, press Open.

6

Trim, then Confirm

Watch it once more. Anything at the start or the end you don’t need? Drag the yellow handles to cut it. Press Confirm, then click the video in the library so it’s selected.

Why: every extra second is credits and one more place for AI to go wrong. Keep only what the video needs.

7

One character per person

Count the people in the video. Press Add your characters and add one picture per person, in the order they appear: her, and her friends if there are more people.

Keep the variety the original had. Different outfits, different hair? Pick different ones too.

Need her pictures? Factory → Add reference → Reference library → her niche: her outfits and her friends.

8

The prompt: 3 lines

AI is like a very smart child: it does exactly what you say, nothing more. Paste this and set the number of images to the number of people:

copy motion and vibe from @Video1 but replace the characters in the video with my characters from @Image1 @Image2 @Image3 Keep the outfits from @Image1 @Image2 @Image3
  • Line 1 keeps the movement and the vibe. No dancing or jumping that wasn’t there.
  • Line 2 puts our characters in place of the people. Image 1 replaces the first person, image 2 the second, and so on.
  • Line 3 makes it use the outfits too, not only the faces.
9

Settings, then Generate

Model: Higgsfield Genjutsu.

Quality: 480p only. Not 720p, not 1080p.

Want higher? Ask K first. Look at the Quality box every time before you press Generate.

Double-check the video, the pictures and the prompt. Press Generate. It takes a few minutes.

10

Watch it, fix it, download

Watch the result all the way through, like a fan.

  • Two people swapped outfits? Fine.
  • Everyone in the same outfit, a face wrong, something AI-looking? Change something before you generate again: an outfit, the order of the pictures, a line of the prompt.

Why: the same settings give the same mistake. Change one thing, then try again.

Good? Press Download.

11

Music

Music is what makes a viewer feel the niche. Three ways:

  • Keep the video’s own music if it already fits.
  • Pick a trending song or a song from her niche: music she would actually listen to. This is flexible. example songs per niche
  • Factory → Song library → search her name → a song from her niche → Download.
  • A song from YouTube: copy the YouTube link, paste it into ezconv.org, download it.

K’s example: the Star Trek Deep Space Nine theme for Kira. A fan recognises it in one second.

12

CapCut: video and music in

Open CapCut → Create project → Import → the video, then the music. Drag both onto the timeline: video on top, music below.

13

Time the music to the hook

Play the video alone and find the hook: the moment you’d stop scrolling (K’s: the doors open). Bring the strongest part of the song in right there.

  • Cut the music where the video ends.
  • Turn the video’s own sound down so the music carries it, but the original sound is still there.
  • Play them together and adjust until it feels right.

Why: the first second decides if someone keeps watching. Sound landing on the hook makes it hit harder.

14

The text hook

The text hook is the words on the video. (The caption is what goes under the post.) Almost every video needs one. How to pick it: the next section, Text hooks.

  • Text → Default text, then type it.
  • A font that fits her niche and is easy to read (see Text hooks). Bold, not too big.
  • An emoji or two if it fits.
  • Place it where it never blocks a face.
15

Compare with the original

Watch the original, then yours. Same hook, same energy, but now it’s hers: her outfits, her music, her text hook. Would a fan of her niche stop on it?

K’s original and finished video, side by side

16

Export, save to Drive

Export from CapCut: 9:16, highest quality. Save it in her Drive folder → Reels (SOP: Google Drive).

Remaking a reference video for your task? Put the original and yours side by side in your task.

05Text hooks

The text hook has a split second to stop someone scrolling. It isn’t decoration: it tells the viewer what they’re looking at, and how to feel about it.

A good text hook Hooks in a millisecond. Short. Read at a glance.
Adds context. It says what’s going on, and ties it to her niche.
Puts the viewer in the scene. The best ones make him imagine himself there.
A bit funny, and always related to the video and the niche.
Never a question on screen. Questions go in the caption under the post.

Example: POV: you’re the captain, and this is your crew ❤️

Why it works: the viewer is a Star Trek fan, a man. He reads it and he’s the captain, in the elevator, and the girls are his crew. He isn’t watching a video any more; he’s in it.

Where to find winning text hooks: the reference accounts on your board, and other winning videos in her niche. Find one that worked on a video like yours, then adapt it to her.

Fonts: any font, as long as it’s very clear. A font that echoes her niche adds context: Sophie (Lord of the Rings): Lucette. Star Trek: a font like the Star Trek logo. Copying a video 1:1? Use its font (K’s was Rubik, bold). the exact font names per niche in CapCut

More winning text hooks (watch them in Kinds of videos, below):

  • Legolas would be proud of me 🧝‍♀️🤍: names the fan’s hero. Instantly his world.
  • POV: You accidentally run into your future LOTR wife in the elevator 🧝‍♀️💍: he’s in the scene, and it’s his fantasy.
  • “What do you wanna watch?” · “I don’t know”: a tiny dialogue everyone has had. Relatable, then the twist.

more winning text hooks per niche, from K

09Rules and nuances

  • Higgsfield quality: 480p only. Not 720p, not 1080p. Want higher? Ask K first.
  • Log in with your Santor Google account (K’s email to practise).
  • Export in CapCut: 9:16, highest quality. (That is CapCut, not Higgsfield.)

anything else not in the Loom

10Done means

  • The number of finished videos your task asks for.
  • Each one: her (and friends if needed) in niche outfits, music that fits, a text hook that stops the scroll and blocks no face.
  • Made at 480p in Higgsfield, unless K said yes to higher.
  • Looks real. Nothing AI-looking.
  • Exported 9:16, saved in her Reels folder in Drive; original and yours side by side in your task.
  • Reviewed with K.

11Common mistakes

  • Generating in 720p or 1080p without K’s yes.
  • Generating again without changing anything.
  • Everyone in the same outfit.
  • Music that misses the hook, or keeps playing after the video.
  • A text hook over a face, or a question on screen.
  • Changing what made the original good.

Added after every review with K
